body:
I'm reading in a set of Latitude and Longitude coordinates, captured by mobile devices in Ireland for an analysis project. In order to match them to location data for machine learning, I need to convert them into the local coordinate systems.

The data is in a CSV file, I am using Pandas to import the file, due to the outstanding negative numbers issue, but I tried reading directly and get similar results. Small errors are being introduced in the process:

So if I read the file using read_csv, I get small adjustments in the lat column. (Ignore the lon column, for now, as it contains all negative numbers.)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8914493/49086806-51962c80-f24d-11e8-8010-e365e197cd74.png)

If I then read the file via Pandas, it reads correctly without altering the values:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8914493/49086854-6ffc2800-f24d-11e8-914e-ea0fa2af9b04.png)

But if I then copy the columns to a GPU data frame, it introduces small errors:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8914493/49086900-928e4100-f24d-11e8-99c4-965065c8a80a.png)

I've attached the CSV file, it isn't confidential.

[irish.zip](https://github.com/rapidsai/cudf/files/2620287/irish.zip)
title: cuDF printing mismatches formatting precision of Pandas DF printing
